title: Customer environment snapshot + deterministic replay harness for on-prem/VPC
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a repeatable harness that captures a customer Private/VPC/on-prem environment snapshot (traffic profile, topology, latency/noise characteristics, model variant config) and replays it deterministically in our lab and in-customer testbeds. Goals: measure tokens/sec and p95 tail latency under representative customer load, detect regressions between runtime/model changes, and generate artifactable reports that map to Console dashboards and CI gates.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Harness can ingest a customer snapshot tarball (network map, sample requests, model cfg) and run a deterministic replay with seedable RNG
2) Outputs include: tokens/sec time series, p50/p95/p99 latencies, request error rates, and KV-cache hit distribution in CSV/JSON that Console can ingest
3) Regression detection: automated comparison with a baseline run using statistical tests and a configurable alert threshold
4) Support for network condition emulation (latency/jitter/loss) via netem profiles pulled from snapshot
5) Repro runs produce <3% variance in tokens/sec when run 3x under the same lab environment
tech_notes: Prototype: python runner that loads normalized request traces and issues requests against a pinned model endpoint in an isolated VPC; uses deterministic seeds for prompt sampling and ordering
We will capture KV cache state where available and allow cache warmup sequences to be re-run as part of the replay
Network emulation: use tc/netem profiles; store profiles in snapshot as human-readable DSL for portability
Determinism trade-off: strict byte-identical reproduction is impossible for some 3rd-party infra; we aim for statistical reproducibility (tokens/sec +/-3%, p95 within margin)
Plan to integrate with CI: runner publishes artifacts to an S3-like bucket and creates a summary JSON used by a regression CI step
Privacy: snapshots must be PII-sanitized; we will include a scrubber step and require customer opt-in before ingesting any snapshot
Security: runner will operate in ephemeral sandboxed test VPCs and use SA keys with least privilege; security review requested
progress_updates: 2025-02-21: Initial spike complete. Implemented trace normalizer and simple replay prototype. Verified basic tokens/sec measurement against local runtime.
2025-02-25: Added deterministic seed support and replay ordering. Seeded sampling reduces variance in token distribution by ~18% across runs.

2025-02-27: First on-prem mirror run (small customer sandbox) executed. Observed p95 regressions vs hosted baseline; root cause appears to be kernel scheduling differences and small packet jitter not modeled in lab.
2025-03-01: Implemented netem profile ingestion and applied jitter+loss profile from customer snapshot. p95 aligned closer to customer capture: reduction of discrepancy from 42ms to 9ms.
2025-03-03: Added basic regression detector (Mann-Whitney U for latency distributions + percentage delta for tokens/sec). Alert thresholds configurable per-run. Draft PR opened.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use statistical reproducibility rather than strict byte-level determinism to keep tool practical across different hardware/OS kernels
Prefer netem-based network emulation and customer-provided profiles over full packet-level replay to keep resource costs reasonable
Cache warmup sequences are stored and replayed deterministically where possible; for opaque customer caches fallback is to measured warmup period in snapshot
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer snapshots may contain sensitive data -> Mitigation: mandatory scrubber and customer opt-in plus ephemeral isolated environments
Risk: Lab hardware scheduling may not match customer on-prem -> Mitigation: annotate snapshot with hardware hints and run topology-aware node selection in the lab
Risk: Non-determinism in token generation for some models -> Mitigation: seed prompt sampling and detect model variance; flag runs as non-deterministic in reports
next_steps: Add Console ingestion: create mapping for summary JSON -> Console regression dash widgets (owner: observability)
Run 5 customer snapshots end-to-end and evaluate false positive rate of regression detector
